In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
imprinting of Igf2R is not a convergent evolution, but rather a common feature among all mammals.
Igf2r was imprinted before the divergence of monotremes and marsupials, but not monotremes and eutherians, and that the regulatory elements required for imprinting were lost in the eutherian lineage.
the imprinting of Igf2 is not a convergent evolution, but rather a common inheritance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Igf2r regulation is not the same in all mammals, but that it does appear to be similar in marsupials and eutherians.
the genomic imprinting status of a gene can be altered by the acquisition and/or loss of cis-regulatory elements.
the genomic elements required for Igf2r imprinted expression in Eutheria are not required for imprinted expression of this gene in the marsupial subclass of mammals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulatory mechanisms that govern the expression of Igf2 and Igf2r are not evolutionarily conserved between marsupials and eutherians.
the imprinting of Igf2R in marsupial mammals is not dependent on the same genomic regulatory elements required for imprinting in eutherian mammals.
the imprinting of Igf2R in the marsupial opossum does not require the CpG2, antisense RNA, or differential methylation of CpG1.
